Principle 05 of 8

Care

Protect vulnerable people; do not profit from distress, grief, or compulsion.

Protects

Children, people in crisis, older adults, anyone vulnerable

Why it matters

Some people cannot protect themselves in the moment. A business that targets that moment is choosing profit over the person.

Covers

Exploitation of vulnerable populations (Category 10), emotional manipulation and engagement-addiction design (3.6–3.8), and crisis pricing and predatory lending (1.2, 1.7).

1.2 Surge & Crisis Pricing · 5 practices

Care+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.2.1Crisis-Period Price GougingAlgorithmically raising prices on essential goods or services during emergencies, weather events, or supply shocks when consumers cannot defer purchase.Grocery, e-commerce, ride-hailing, food delivery, plumbing/home repair, pest control
1.2.2Emergency-Markup ExploitationCharging premium rates for after-hours, urgent, or emergency service when the customer has no time to compare alternatives.Plumbing, automotive towing, veterinary, healthcare, funeral services, cybersecurity (ransomware response)
1.2.3Last-Minute Price InflationRaising prices dramatically as the deadline (travel date, event, deadline) approaches, exploiting urgency.Travel, ticketing, gambling, betting
1.2.4Algorithmic Personalized PricingAdjusting prices in real time based on browsing history, device, location, or perceived willingness to pay without disclosure.Hospitality, e-commerce, ride-hailing, grocery, fashion, ticketing
1.2.5Tourist-Targeted OverchargingCharging higher prices to visibly identifiable visitors who lack local knowledge of fair prices, sometimes refusing meters or quoting opaque flat rates.Taxi services, retail in tourist zones, hospitality, currency exchange
